spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact canonicalization table from whatwg/html#12898 — safe preset false, bare dictionary true, explicit values preserved — plus the setJavascriptURLs changed/no-op return contract, all read back through the real get().

interactive.rationale: A run button constructs four real Sanitizer instances, fills the comparison table from get(), and executes the mutator sequence; nothing is precomputed.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the four constructions, the two defaulting rules and the mutator contract; the page delivers each as its own panel/row.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers no-Sanitizer-at-all, option-not-implemented (member absent from get(), mutator absent — explicitly refusing to read an ignored unknown dictionary member as support), reflected-but-divergent, and the fully-conformant state.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5169798320357376 and whatwg/html#12898 on the page; the feature index adds the HTML-standard section and MDN.

conformance.rationale: New 8-assertion feature suite mirrors the same contracts (presence, three canonicalizations, return contract, strip/keep behavior, non-navigating scope); on this container's flag-enabled Chromium 141 it reads 0 pass / 8 fail — the honest pre-157 answer.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 with --enable-blink-features=SanitizerAPI via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): run button clicked, all four rows filled with 'absent from get() — option not implemented', verdict took the honest not-implemented branch, mutator panel reported typeof undefined, zero console errors, zero failed requests, 0px overflow, desktop screenshot read. Partial: the 157 implemented path could not execute on this build.

telemetry_health.rationale: sanitizer-jsurls-readback-ran asserts the table filled; the mutator-contract assert only fires when the mutator exists; the no-API branch has its own assert.

design_system.rationale: Table value colors (blue keep / emerald strip / rose missing) sit on bg-paper at AA; buttons keep the paired background+color override.

accessibility.rationale: Native button, caption + th scope table inside an overflow wrapper, verdict is aria-live=polite, mutator output is a plain output element updated once per run.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: responsive-check matrix run for the feature id: mobile 360×740 DPR3 and desktop 1280×800, no horizontal overflow, console/network clean, both screenshots read; the table scrolls inside .table-wrap on narrow widths.

openQuestions.title: Verify the four canonicalizations on Chrome 157+
openQuestions.detail: On a 157+ build, confirm the table reads false/true/true/false, the verdict goes green, the mutator sequence reports [true,false,true] with final false, and the conformance route reaches 8/8.

guidanceConsulted.query: sanitize untrusted HTML safely display output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use setHTML for safe insertion; safe methods cannot be made more permissive for XSS-unsafe content; custom configs only restrict further.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The page frames javascriptURLs as the one regularised exception to that method-decides model and keeps all sanitizer output inside detached nodes read back as data, never mounted.

guidanceConsulted.query: comparison table of API results accessible markup
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Semantic table with caption and th scope inside an overflow wrapper; one polite live region for the outcome.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The readback table uses caption + scoped headers in .table-wrap; the verdict paragraph is the single aria-live region.

summary: Canonicalization probe: four real constructions read back via get(), the setJavascriptURLs return contract, and detection that refuses to treat an ignored dictionary member as support. Driven on flag-enabled headless Chromium 141 (repo CDP harness; no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment): honest not-implemented branch everywhere, clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
